tasks.short: Issue room keys and escort instructions to bellhops.

steps.what: Issue room keys to the guest in person.
Note which room keys were just issued.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk issues the key and gives the escort instructions to the bellhop in person. A short note on {OPS_SYSTEM} records which key left the desk. No message is sent in place of the handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: The key and the escort were already done in person, and a paper key log was easy to skip.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system can hold a key number next to the room the clerk has just assigned.
tasks.still_hard: A lock can fail, a guest can need a second key, and the bellhop has to hear the instruction from a person.
tasks.human_edge: Handing over a key and telling a bellhop where to go stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: Almost all of this stays at the desk. The note of which key left is the only shorter piece, and the clerk still checks it.

reach.learn: Take the instruction from the desk clerk in person

evidence.claim: A key number can be stored against a room after the clerk has issued the key.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the room is assigned and ends when the guest has the key. Lock changes and lost-key incidents stay outside it.
The note fields are room number, key number, and time. The clerk produces them. There is no send to the bellhop.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. The note does not replace issuing the key.
Upkeep is a short check that key numbers still match rooms.
unknowns: Whether keys are physical, coded cards, or both.
Whether the property already logs a card when it is encoded.
research_questions: Are room keys physical keys, coded cards, or both?
Does encoding a card already write a log line?

already_counted.description: Noting the key number stays mostly in that step

incremental.description: Check that key numbers still match rooms

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case is the one that already applies: issuing the key and instructing the bellhop do not shrink. The low end drops only the small note, and only if that note is still typed by hand. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise housekeeping which vacated rooms are ready.

steps.what: See which rooms have been vacated.
Decide the vacated rooms are ready for cleaning.
Advise housekeeping staff which rooms are ready.
Send the vacated-room note the clerk advised.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk sees departures on {OPS_SYSTEM}, decides which rooms are ready, and advises housekeeping in person. A note of those same rooms is sent only after that advice. The note does not decide that a room is ready.
tasks.previous_blocker: The advice was a phone call, and the same room numbers were then written again for the housekeeper.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system already knows which stays have departed, so a list the clerk has accepted can be sent without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A guest may still be in the room, and a do-not-disturb sign can make a departed room not ready.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk decides that a room is ready and tells housekeeping. A list is not that advice.
tasks.altitude: Seeing departures is a bit shorter. Deciding a room is ready, and advising housekeeping, stay with the clerk.

reach.learn: Start from the rooms the desk clerk has advised are ready

evidence.claim: A list of room numbers the clerk has marked ready can be sent to housekeeping.
Saying a room is ready for someone to enter is the clerk's decision, made after they have seen the departure.

assumptions: The workflow starts at departure and ends when the accepted room list is sent. The cleaning itself stays outside it.
The note fields are room numbers and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the ready mark. A room the clerk has not marked is not sent.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the advice. Only the second copy of the room list is a send.
Upkeep is keeping the departure status that the desk is allowed to trust.
unknowns: Whether housekeeping already sees departures without a note from the desk.
How the desk learns that a guest has left when the departure was not recorded.
research_questions: Does housekeeping already see departed rooms in the property system?
What should the desk do when a room shows departed but the guest is still there?

already_counted.description: Seeing which rooms are vacated stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep the departure status the desk trusts

approvals.approved_version: vacated rooms the hotel desk clerk advised are ready for cleaning

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If housekeeping already sees departures, the send is unused and the low end is the clerk still deciding and still advising in person. The list never goes out ahead of that advice. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Write the message in the clerk's own words.
Review the written message before any transmit.
Transmit the messages the clerk wrote.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk hears the caller and writes the message. The clerk reviews that writing. {OPS_SYSTEM} then transmits that accepted text. Calls are not transcribed, and no message is sent that the clerk did not write.
tasks.previous_blocker: The message was written on a slip and then read out or retyped for the guest.
tasks.enabler_now: A short text the clerk has written can be delivered on the stay without a second copy.
tasks.still_hard: The caller may be unclear, the guest may be out, and a message about a medical or legal matter needs the clerk's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears the caller and chooses the words. A delivery is not a new message.
tasks.altitude: Hearing the caller and writing the words stay. Delivering the text the clerk already wrote takes less of a second copy.

reach.task: Read a message left at the desk
reach.learn: Receive only the words the desk clerk wrote and accepted

evidence.claim: A short message the clerk has written can be delivered onto the guest's stay.
Recording a telephone call, or sending words the clerk did not write, is not part of this task.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a caller leaves a message and ends when the accepted text is delivered. Emergency calls and switchboard operation stay outside it.
The fields are stay id, the clerk's text, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the text. There is no transcript. If the clerk does not accept the text, nothing is sent.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on hearing and writing. Only the delivery of an accepted text is a send.
Upkeep is keeping the delivery path to the stay, not a script of calls.
unknowns: Whether the property already delivers a slip without a second system.
Whether works-council rules allow any record of the call itself. This design does not record the call.
research_questions: How are telephone messages delivered to the guest today?
Is any recording of desk calls already in place, and who agreed to it?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the clerk's own wording stays mostly in that step

incremental.description: Keep the path that delivers a message onto a stay

approvals.approved_version: message the hotel desk clerk wrote before it was transmitted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If messages stay on paper slips, the send is not built and the low end is the clerk still hearing and still writing. No call is transcribed in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record guest complaints and refer them to managers.

steps.what: Hear guest comments or complaints at the desk.
Decide on referring customers to managers.
Walk the guest to a manager when referring.
Review the record of guest complaints.

loop.input: The comments the clerk logged and the referral decision the clerk already made
loop.output: A short record that repeats only those words and says whether a manager was asked
loop.check: The clerk rejects any sentence that adds a fact they did not log
loop.stop: One draft, at most 80 words. If a fact is missing, that line stays blank. No second pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: Complaint wording is free text, so a fixed line cannot start from what the guest said

steps.what: File the record of complaints the clerk accepted.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk hears the guest, decides on referring them to a manager, and does that referral in person. A draft arranges only the words the clerk logged. The clerk reviews it. {WORKFLOW} files the accepted record and does not decide the referral.
tasks.previous_blocker: The complaint was written twice, once for the guest and once for the manager, after the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: A register can store a note the clerk has accepted, next to the stay.
tasks.still_hard: The guest is still in front of the clerk, and the decision to involve a manager depends on what was just said.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears the guest and decides on referring them. A filed note is not the referral.
tasks.altitude: Hearing the guest, deciding on a referral, and walking them to a manager stay. Filing the accepted note takes less retyping.

reach.task: Take a guest the desk has referred
reach.learn: Read the note only after the desk clerk has accepted it

evidence.claim: A complaint note can be drafted from words the clerk logged, then filed after the clerk checks it.
Deciding to refer a guest to a manager is the clerk's decision and stays in person.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest comments and ends when the accepted note is filed. Compensation and any legal claim stay outside it.

The fields are stay id, the clerk's words, whether a manager was asked, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the words and the referral. Spoken words are typed by the clerk. Nothing is taken from a recording.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the hearing and the referral. The draft does not choose the referral.
Upkeep is keeping complaint categories the desk is allowed to use.
unknowns: Whether managers already receive the guest without a filed note.
Whether a works-council check is required before notes that name staff are kept.
research_questions: What must a complaint note contain before a manager will act on it?
May notes that name a staff member be kept, and for how long?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the drafted complaint record stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep complaint categories the desk may use

approvals.approved_version: complaint record the hotel desk clerk accepted after hearing the guest

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the manager takes the guest with no note, the file is unused and the low end is the conversation and the referral, which stay in full. The draft never decides the referral. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keys, escort instructions, hearing a caller, and referring a guest to a manager stay in person. A vacated-room list, a written message, and a complaint note go out only after the clerk has accepted that version.
reach: Housekeeping starts from rooms the desk clerk has advised are ready
A manager reads a complaint note only after the desk clerk has accepted it
skills_to_grow: Advising housekeeping before a room list is sent
Writing a telephone message in their own words, with no transcript
Referring a guest in person before a complaint note is filed
role.ambitious_version: A room list, a guest message, and a complaint note leave the desk only in the version the clerk accepted.

job.title: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
